title: Rolling motion
examples: What is the difference between sliding and rolling?
How does the moment of inertia affect rolling speed?
Can you explain the energy conservation in rolling?

explain.say: Today we look at rolling motion without slipping.

items: Motion involves both sliding and turning
No slipping means contact point is stationary
This condition is key for energy analysis

explain.say: When an object rolls without slipping, its total energy is conserved.
The total kinetic energy has two parts. One is from moving forward.
For rolling without slipping, the angular velocity relates to linear speed.
Consider a solid cylinder rolling down an incline. It has mass and radius.
In reality, rolling objects reach the bottom faster than sliding objects.

draw.text: Rolling is more efficient than sliding

faq.q: Does 'rolling without slipping' mean the object stops moving?
faq.a: No, it means the point of contact with the ground is momentarily at rest. The object is still moving forward and spinning.
asks: What does the no-slip condition mean?

faq.q: If I roll a ball and slide a block, which one has more energy at the bottom?
faq.a: The rolling ball will have its energy distributed between translational and rotational forms. The sliding block will have all its energy as translational kinetic energy.
asks: How does the type of motion affect energy?

faq.q: What is the formula relating linear speed and angular velocity?
faq.a: The relationship is that the linear speed, v, equals the radius times the angular velocity, r times omega. This is a direct link between the two motions.
asks: How are v and ω connected?

faq.q: Does the object's shape change the final speed?
faq.a: Yes, the object's shape determines its moment of inertia, which changes how much energy is stored in rotation versus translation. A sphere rolls differently than a cylinder.
asks: Does the moment of inertia matter?
Does the object's mass affect the speed?

faq.q: Is energy always conserved when rolling down a slope?
faq.a: Yes, assuming no friction or air resistance, the total mechanical energy, which is the sum of potential and kinetic energy, remains constant throughout the roll.
asks: What are the assumptions for energy conservation?
Can energy be lost during rolling?

facts: Rolling without slipping means the point of contact has zero instantaneous velocity.
The total kinetic energy is the sum of translational and rotational kinetic energy.
The relationship between linear speed (v) and angular velocity (ω) is v equals r times ω.
Objects with a larger moment of inertia store more energy in rotation.

quiz.say: A solid sphere and a solid cylinder roll down the same ramp from the same height. Which reaches the bottom first?

options.show: The cylinder will reach the bottom first.
options.say: The cylinder will reach the bottom first.

options.show: They will reach at the same time.
options.say: They will reach at the same time.

options.show: The one with the larger radius wins.
options.say: The one with the larger radius wins.

options.show: The sphere will reach the bottom first.
options.say: The sphere will reach the bottom first.

quiz.why: The sphere has a smaller moment of inertia relative to its mass compared to the cylinder, meaning more energy goes into faster translation.

wrong.0: This is tempting because the cylinder might seem heavier or more solid, but the moment of inertia is the deciding factor.
wrong.1: This assumes only potential energy converts to kinetic energy, ignoring the difference in rotational energy storage.
wrong.2: The radius is only part of the equation; the moment of inertia is the critical factor here.

quiz.say: If an object rolls, its total kinetic energy is composed of which two types of energy?

options.show: Only potential energy and translational kinetic energy.
options.say: Only potential energy and translational kinetic energy.

options.show: Only rotational kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy.
options.say: Only rotational kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy.

options.show: Translational kinetic energy and rotational kinetic energy.
options.say: Translational kinetic energy and rotational kinetic energy.

quiz.why: Rolling motion inherently involves both movement of the center of mass and spinning around the center of mass.

wrong.0: This forgets the energy stored in the object's spin, which is crucial for rolling.
wrong.1: This ignores the forward movement of the center of mass, which is the translation part.
wrong.2: Energy is converted, not just held; the final kinetic energy is the result of this conversion.

quiz.say: A wheel rolls down a ramp. If its mass is m, radius is r, and it rolls at speed v, what is the total kinetic energy?
quiz.why: We substitute ω with v/r into the rotational term to get everything in terms of linear speed v.

wrong.1: This only accounts for the energy of the center of mass, ignoring the spin.
wrong.2: This is correct but doesn't use the relationship v = rω to express it fully in terms of v.
wrong.3: This is the initial potential energy, not the final kinetic energy at the bottom.
